material_systems.name: Interior Adhesion Primer for Previously Painted Cabinets
material_systems.description: Water-based adhesion promoter for previously painted cabinet surfaces. Bonds to glossy, chalky, or oil-based existing coatings without full mechanical sanding. Primary RP primer for sound-oil-based, failing, and peeling conditions. Kitchen cabinets historically received oil-based enamel (semi-gloss/gloss default sheen) making adhesion primer especially critical when solvent test confirms alkyd base. Also required when adhesion test is marginal on any existing finish type.

applies_when.notes: For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT + painted_oil: MANDATORY (latex-over-oil compatibility). For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT + painted_latex: conditional — skip if adhesion test passes on low-sheen surfaces; apply if marginal adhesion or existing sheen is semi-gloss+. For SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT and SS_INT_PEELING: always apply regardless of factory_finish_type.

products.notes: Water-based for low VOC and easy cleanup. Bonds to glossy surfaces without full mechanical sanding. For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT + painted_oil: MANDATORY — latex-over-oil requires bonding agent. For SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT + painted_latex: use only when adhesion test is marginal or existing sheen is semi-gloss+. For SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas, full prime if bare >30%. For SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime after complete scrape.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT: conditional — skip if adhesion test passes AND existing coating is latex AND low sheen; MANDATORY if existing coating is oil-based, marginal adhesion, or high-sheen existing finish
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped areas (<30% bare) or full prime (>=30% bare)
prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_PEELING: full surface prime — extensive bare area after complete scrape

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Bonding Primer for Factory Lacquer/Catalyzed Varnish/Thermofoil
material_systems.description: Enhanced bonding primer for factory-finished cabinet surfaces that are extremely hard and non-porous. Factory lacquer (common on 1990s-2000s oak cabinets), catalyzed conversion varnish (modern high-end), and intact thermofoil (vinyl-wrapped MDF) all require bonding primer because standard primers have zero mechanical or chemical adhesion to these surfaces. DISTINCT from SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT — same products but different routing logic (factory finish type driven rather than condition driven). Thermofoil requires adhesion test gate BEFORE priming.

applies_when.notes: Routing is factory-finish-type-driven, NOT condition-driven. Factory lacquer/catalyzed varnish: bonding primer mandatory regardless of condition. Thermofoil: bonding primer after adhesion test gate (go/no-go — delaminating thermofoil is NOT paintable). unknown: defaults to bonding primer (safest). Any substrate_state can trigger this system when factory_finish_type matches.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Stix Waterborne Bonding Primer
products.notes: Same products as SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT but used for factory-finish bonding rather than condition-driven adhesion. Factory lacquer is extremely hard and slick — standard primer will not adhere. Thermofoil requires mechanical scuff with 120-grit (NOT chemical degloss — solvents damage vinyl) followed by bonding primer. ASTM D3359 adhesion test on bonding primer before proceeding to finish coats.

prime_scope_by_state.lacquer: full surface prime — mandatory, factory lacquer is impervious to standard primers
prime_scope_by_state.catalyzed_varnish: full surface prime — mandatory, catalyzed finish is extremely hard
prime_scope_by_state.thermofoil: full surface prime AFTER adhesion test gate passes — if thermofoil is delaminating, STOP (replacement required, not paintable)
prime_scope_by_state.unknown: full surface prime — default to bonding primer when finish type cannot be identified

thermofoil_gate.description: Go/no-go assessment gate for thermofoil cabinets. Inspect all edges, corners, and heat-exposed areas (near oven, dishwasher) for lifting/bubbling. If any delamination found, cabinet is NOT paintable — replacement required.
thermofoil_gate.prep_requirement: 120-grit mechanical scuff only. NO chemical degloss — solvents damage vinyl wrap.
thermofoil_gate.adhesion_test: ASTM D3359 cross-hatch test on bonding primer — must pass before proceeding to finish coats.

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Interior Stain-Blocking Primer (Shellac-Based)
material_systems.description: Shellac-based stain blocker for smoke-damaged cabinets. Full-surface application required — smoke contamination is pervasive even when not visually apparent. Kitchen cabinets trap concentrated smoke/nicotine deposits in door profile crevices, frame joints, and cabinet interiors. Cooking grease carbonization creates a compound contamination layer (grease + smoke) that only shellac can reliably seal. Latex and acrylic primers have ZERO stain blocking capability (RC-002).

products.notes: Shellac is the ONLY product that reliably seals nicotine/smoke residue. Full surface application required. Strong odor — requires ventilation. Fast dry (~45 min recoat). NOT water-cleanup — requires denatured alcohol for tool cleaning. Door profile crevices and cabinet interior corners trap concentrated smoke deposits — ensure full coverage of all profile details. Two coats BIN for heavy nicotine.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE: full surface — mandatory, no exceptions. Smoke contamination extends beyond visible damage.

material_systems.cleanup: Denatured alcohol. Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. CON_DENATURED_ALCOHOL required.

material_systems.name: Interior Mildew-Resistant Primer for Moisture-Damaged Cabinets
material_systems.description: Mildew-resistant primer with antimicrobial additives for moisture-damaged cabinet surfaces. Applied after biocide treatment and full drying. Most common on under-sink base cabinet interiors where plumbing leaks create moisture intrusion, and bathroom vanity cabinets exposed to humidity. Gate condition: moisture SOURCE must be resolved before painting — painting over active leak causes accelerated failure.

products.notes: Apply only after biocide treatment (CON_BIOCIDE_SPRAY) and full drying (24+ hrs). Contains antimicrobial additives preventing spore regrowth under paint film. Gate condition: active moisture source MUST be resolved by other trades. Under-sink cabinet floors/back walls and bathroom vanity surrounds are primary application areas.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE: full surface prime on all affected areas — mildew spores may be present beyond visible damage area

material_systems.cleanup: Water cleanup. Standard latex cleanup procedure.

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: 100% acrylic enamel for standard residential cabinet repaint at QT3. Fast dry/recoat, non-yellowing, water cleanup. Standard production grade. Same product selection as NC cabinet and door finish. Lower hardness than alkyd — blocking risk on cabinet doors (door-to-frame contact). Adequate for production work but not ideal for high-traffic kitchen cabinets. Cabinet interiors always use this system regardless of exterior tier (AWI semi-exposed standard).

example_products: Sherwin-Williams ProClassic Waterborne Interior Acrylic Enamel (B31)
Benjamin Moore Regal Select Interior Semi-Gloss (N551)
products.notes: Fast dry/recoat. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Standard production grade. Lower hardness than alkyd — monitor for blocking on door-to-frame contact. Cabinet interiors always use this system regardless of exterior tier per AWI semi-exposed standard.

material_systems.notes: QT3 — satin maximum per Fine Finish Doctrine SS4.1. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion on product selection.

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Urethane-modified alkyd / waterbased alkyd for premium residential cabinet repaint at QT4. Superior flow and leveling, harder cured film. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Do not overwork. Blocking resistant — ideal for cabinet doors. Extended cure time (7+ days full hardness) — cabinet door/drawer reinstall timing critical. STRONGLY recommended over standard acrylic for ALL cabinet work.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Advance Waterborne Interior Alkyd (N794)
Sherwin-Williams Pro Industrial Waterbased Alkyd Urethane (B53)
products.notes: Superior flow and leveling. Harder cured film. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Do not overwork. Blocking resistant — ideal for cabinet door-to-frame contact. Extended cure time (7-14 days full hardness) — coordinate door/drawer reinstall timing at Visit 2.

material_systems.notes: QT4. STRONGLY recommended over standard acrylic for all cabinet work. Semi-gloss is traditional/default kitchen cabinet sheen at this tier. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion.

material_systems.name: Premium Urethane Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Premium acrylic-urethane enamel for superior cabinet repaint at QT5. Maximum durability, excellent leveling, hardest film. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Sands easily between coats.

products.coat_notes: QT5 brush method typically requires 3+ coats per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 spray: 2 coats standard.
products.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Hardest film. SHORT working time — apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd (RC-006). Sands easily between coats.

material_systems.notes: QT5. Gloss available only at this tier. Premium product mandatory at QT5. Material systems are recommendations — contractor has discretion.

ITM_CABINET_DOOR.notes: Average cabinet door face ~6 SF. Previously painted substrate absorbs less primer than bare wood. Higher coverage than NC bare-wood primer (350-400 SF/gal).

ITM_CABINET_DRAWER.notes: Average drawer front face ~3 SF. Same coverage rate as doors — previously painted surface.

ITM_CABINET_FRAME.notes: Measured directly in SF from PaintScope. Previously painted surface — higher coverage than NC bare-wood primer.

ITM_CABINET_INTERIOR.notes: Measured directly in SF from PaintScope. Slightly lower coverage than exterior surfaces due to enclosed box geometry increasing spray waste (20-30%).

coverage_profiles.notes: Adhesion primer on previously painted cabinet surfaces. Lower porosity than bare wood results in higher coverage vs NC primer profiles (COV_CABT_PRIMER at 400 SF/gal). Coverage is consistent across door types for primer — complexity modifier does not affect primer coverage significantly.
assumptions: Previously painted substrate — lower absorption than bare wood
Standard cabinet door ~6 SF, drawer ~3 SF per face
Door type complexity does not significantly affect primer coverage rate

ITM_CABINET_DOOR.notes: Factory finish surfaces are non-porous — higher coverage than adhesion primer on painted surfaces.

ITM_CABINET_DRAWER.notes: Same non-porous surface coverage as doors.

ITM_CABINET_FRAME.notes: Factory lacquer/catalyzed varnish frames have extremely low absorption — bonding primer sits on surface.

ITM_CABINET_INTERIOR.notes: Slightly lower than exterior due to enclosed box spray waste. Factory-finished interiors are less common — most factory finishes are on exterior surfaces.

coverage_profiles.notes: Bonding primer on factory lacquer, catalyzed varnish, and thermofoil surfaces. Non-porous substrates result in highest coverage of any primer profile. Material sits on surface rather than absorbing.
assumptions: Factory finish surfaces are non-porous — minimal absorption
Coverage 10-15% higher than adhesion primer on painted surfaces

ITM_CABINET_DOOR.notes: Shellac stain blocker has lower coverage due to higher solids content. Door profile crevices (rail-stile joints, panel recesses) trap concentrated smoke deposits requiring heavier application.

ITM_CABINET_FRAME.notes: Frame joints and corner crevices trap smoke residue requiring thorough coverage. Lower coverage than latex primers.

ITM_CABINET_INTERIOR.notes: Cabinet interiors concentrate smoke/nicotine deposits in enclosed boxes. Heavier application required + spray waste in enclosed geometry.

coverage_profiles.notes: Shellac-based stain blocker has lower coverage than latex primers due to higher solids content and heavier required film build. Full surface application required on smoke-damaged cabinets. Two coats may be needed for heavy nicotine.
assumptions: Full surface application on smoke-damaged cabinets
Shellac products have higher solids, lower spread rate than latex
Cabinet interiors require heaviest application due to concentrated smoke deposits
Panel door crevices require additional material

ITM_CABINET_DOOR.notes: Mildew primer coverage similar to adhesion primer — latex-based formula. Door application is uncommon; moisture damage typically concentrates at base cabinet interior.

ITM_CABINET_DRAWER.notes: Drawer front mildew priming is rare — included for completeness.

ITM_CABINET_FRAME.notes: Frame base sections near floor and sink area. Slightly thicker film build for antimicrobial effectiveness.

ITM_CABINET_INTERIOR.notes: Primary target — under-sink cabinet interiors and bath vanity interiors. Slightly lower coverage due to thicker recommended film build + enclosed box spray waste.

coverage_profiles.notes: Mildew-resistant primer coverage similar to adhesion primer (latex-based formula). Slightly thicker recommended film build for antimicrobial effectiveness. Primary target is under-sink base cabinet interiors and bathroom vanity surrounds.
assumptions: Latex formula — similar coverage to adhesion primer
Slightly thicker film build for antimicrobial effectiveness
Cabinet interiors are primary application target

slab.notes: Flat panel — minimal material waste, no crevices. Slightly higher coverage.

raised_panel.notes: Recessed areas and profile details reduce coverage. Material settles in panel crevices.

glass_frame.notes: Narrow frame members — less surface area per unit but fiddly application.

ITM_CABINET_DOOR.notes: Finish coat on primed/prepared door surface. Door style affects coverage rate — raised_panel doors consume ~10% more material than standard average.

ITM_CABINET_DRAWER.notes: Finish coat on primed/prepared drawer front. Same per-SF coverage rate as doors. Door style modifier applies to drawers equally.

ITM_CABINET_FRAME.notes: Finish coat on primed/prepared frame surface. Equivalent to NC frame finish coverage (COV_CABT_FINISH at 400 SF/gal) because substrate condition after prime is equivalent.

ITM_CABINET_INTERIOR.notes: Finish coat on cabinet interior. Add 20-30% spray waste for enclosed boxes. Always QT3/SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC regardless of exterior tier.

coverage_profiles.notes: Finish coat coverage on primed cabinet surfaces. After priming, substrate condition is equivalent to NC — coverage rates match NC profiles. Door style affects coverage (raised_panel 10% more material, slab 10% less). Coat count: QT3-QT4 = 2 coats, QT5 brush = 3 coats per FFD 15.10.3.
assumptions: Primed smooth surface — equivalent to NC after prime
Standard cabinet door ~6 SF, drawer ~3 SF per face
Two-coat system standard; third coat at QT5 brush has same per-coat coverage
Cabinet interior spray waste 20-30% increases effective material consumption

consumables.name: RP Assessment Kit (adhesion test + coating ID + moisture)
consumables.specification: Cross-hatch cutter, pressure-sensitive tape (ASTM D3359), mineral spirits, xylene, denatured alcohol, acetone, white rags, pin-type moisture meter for coating identification and adhesion testing
consumables.notes: RP-specific assessment supplies. One kit per project. Includes ASTM D3359 cross-hatch adhesion test materials, 4-solvent test supplies for coating ID (mineral spirits dissolves alkyd, xylene softens lacquer, denatured alcohol dissolves shellac, acetone softens latex). Cabinets require the FULL 4-solvent test — more complex than door/trim coating ID due to factory lacquer/catalyzed varnish possibilities. Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: TSP (Trisodium Phosphate) Cleaner / Kitchen Degreaser
consumables.specification: Powdered or liquid TSP concentrate, mixed per manufacturer directions. Alternative: TSP substitute for restricted jurisdictions
consumables.notes: Cabinet RP PRIMARY USE CASE. Required for kitchen cabinet grease/cooking oil removal before any sanding or priming. One quart of concentrate makes enough solution for ~2 kitchen rooms (standard and complex layouts). Multiple wash passes may be needed for heavy grease accumulation above range and near cooktop. Verify clean by wiping with white cloth — if cloth comes back discolored, re-wash. Not used in NC (new substrate is clean).

consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Deglosser
consumables.specification: Liquid sander/deglosser for chemical degloss of existing paint, Krud Kutter Gloss-Off, Wilbond, or equivalent
consumables.notes: RP-specific: chemical degloss for existing semi-gloss/gloss cabinet finishes. Alternative to mechanical sanding for profiled doors (raised_panel, shaker) where sandpaper cannot reach all recessed areas. Especially valuable for factory lacquer surfaces that are too hard for effective mechanical scuff. NOT applicable to thermofoil — solvents damage vinyl wrap. One quart covers ~150 SF (mix of frame/door surfaces). Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Heavy-Duty Kitchen Cabinet Degreaser
consumables.specification: Concentrated kitchen degreaser for heavy grease accumulation, Krud Kutter Kitchen Degreaser All-Purpose Cleaner or equivalent
consumables.notes: Cabinet-specific: for heavy grease accumulation on cabinets above range, near cooktop, and vent hood area where TSP alone is insufficient. Stronger formulation than TSP for carbonized cooking grease. Use before TSP wash as a targeted pre-treatment on heaviest grease areas. One quart per kitchen for targeted treatment. Not needed for bathroom vanity cabinets (no cooking grease).

consumables.name: Mildew Biocide Treatment Spray
consumables.specification: Mildew biocide spray, Concrobium Mold Control or equivalent antimicrobial treatment
consumables.notes: RP-conditional: for SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE under-sink and bath vanity cabinets with active or historic mildew. Apply 24+ hours before priming. Kills spores and prevents regrowth. Gate: moisture source must be resolved before treatment. One quart treats ~100 SF of affected surface. Shared across interior RP specs.

consumables.name: Wood Hardener / Consolidant
consumables.specification: Penetrating wood consolidant, Minwax Wood Hardener or equivalent
consumables.notes: For moisture-damaged cabinet base floors and back walls where wood substrate is softened. Penetrating consolidant stabilizes wood fibers before filling/priming. Conditional on SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE + soft substrate finding during assessment. Under-sink cabinet floors and bath vanity bases are primary use case.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 120-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 120 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: Aggressive grit for feathering scrape edges on failing/peeling cabinets and mechanical scuff on factory lacquer/thermofoil surfaces. Creates smooth transition from scraped to sound paint. Also used for thermofoil mechanical scuff (ONLY method — chemical degloss damages vinyl). One sheet covers ~15 SF.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 150 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: General prep grit for mechanical degloss/scuff sanding on existing cabinet finishes. All tiers. Used on factory lacquer and catalyzed varnish surfaces where aggressive mechanical scuff is required. One sheet per ~15 SF.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 180-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 180 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: Medium prep grit for standard degloss scuff on previously painted (latex) surfaces. All tiers. One sheet per ~15 SF.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 220 grit, 9x11 inch

grit_by_tier.QT3: 220 — spot sand nibs and rough spots only between coats
grit_by_tier.QT4: 220 — full surface sand for adhesion and leveling between coats

consumables.notes: Interstage sanding between finish coats and light sand of primer before finish. Spot sand at QT3, full surface at QT4. One sheet per ~12 SF (lower yield than prep sand due to finer grit loading faster). Rigid sanding block mandatory for flat surfaces per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320-grit
consumables.specification: Sandpaper sheet, 320 grit, 9x11 inch
consumables.notes: QT5 interstage sanding between finish coats. Thorough 320-grit sanding per FFD 15.10.3. Uniform scratch pattern required. One sheet per ~10 SF (finer grit loads fastest). Rigid sanding block mandatory per FFD 15.4.1.

consumables.name: Contour Sanding Sponge
consumables.specification: Flexible sanding sponge, medium/fine grit (150-220), angled edges for profile conformance
consumables.notes: Flexible sanding sponge for profiled cabinet door prep and interstage. Conforms to rail-stile joints, raised panel bevels, shaker recesses, and frame inside corners where rigid blocks cannot reach. Essential for shaker, raised_panel, and glass_frame doors. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine: flexible sponges for profile-following only, NOT for defect leveling (use rigid block for flat surfaces). One sponge per ~30 doors.

consumables.name: Sanding block (fine grit range)
consumables.specification: Rigid sanding block, fine grit range (150-220)
consumables.notes: Rigid blocks remove defects — mandatory per FFD 15.4.1 for between-coat sanding on flat cabinet surfaces (door slab field, drawer front, frame stile/rail flats). Flexible sponges are NOT acceptable for defect leveling. One per crew, reusable across coats.

consumables.name: Tack cloth
consumables.specification: Resin-impregnated cheesecloth for dust removal
consumables.notes: Wipe cabinet surfaces immediately before each coat application to remove sanding dust. Essential for quality finish per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.12. One tack cloth covers ~8 cabinet doors (smaller surface per unit than full-size doors). Use before every coat for dust-free surface.

consumables.name: Lightweight spackling compound
consumables.specification: Lightweight spackling compound, tub or squeeze tube
consumables.notes: For patching scrape edges, filling gouges, and repairing dings/scratches/impact damage on RP cabinets. GOOD condition typically has no fill work. FAIR/POOR condition: fill scraped transition areas, surface defects, small dents, and hardware relocation holes. One quart per ~100 SF of affected surface.

consumables.name: Sandable wood filler
consumables.specification: Sandable wood filler, stainable not required (painting over)
consumables.notes: For deeper damage repair — deep scratches, impact damage, hardware screw hole fill when relocating hardware. Structural fill where lightweight spackle is insufficient. One quart per ~100 SF of affected surface.

consumables.name: Paintable acrylic latex caulk
consumables.specification: Paintable acrylic latex caulk, white, 10.1 oz tube
consumables.notes: For caulk assess/replace at cabinet-to-wall joints on RP cabinets. RP caulk replacement is selective — assess each joint, replace only deteriorated sections (cracked, separated, discolored, mildewed). ~15-30% of joints need replacement in typical RP. One tube covers ~72 LF. Allow cure time before coating.

consumables.name: Caulk gun
consumables.specification: Standard caulk gun, ratchet-type
consumables.notes: Reusable tool for caulk application. One per crew.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (2-2.5 inch)
consumables.specification: 2-2.5 inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle (nylon/polyester blend)
consumables.notes: Primary brush application tool for cabinet finish and primer. One per painter per material type (primer brush + finish brush). Also used for touch-up/detail work with spray method. Quality brush essential for smooth finish on cabinets — scrutinized surface.

consumables.name: Angled sash brush (1.5 inch) for detail
consumables.specification: 1.5 inch angled sash brush, synthetic bristle, for panel crevice and frame stop detail
consumables.notes: Smaller detail brush for profiled cabinet door crevices (rail-stile joints, panel recess corners, shaker inner edges), frame inside corners, and tight areas behind plumbing. One per material type when profiled doors are in scope.

consumables.name: Brush for shellac (dedicated)
consumables.specification: 2-inch angled sash brush, dedicated for shellac use, natural or synthetic bristle
consumables.notes: Dedicated brush for shellac stain-blocking primer (BIN). Shellac requires alcohol cleanup — keep separate from latex brushes. Conditional on smoke damage substrate state.

consumables.name: Mini foam/microfiber roller (4-inch)
consumables.specification: 4-inch mini foam or microfiber roller cover, 3/16 to 1/4 inch nap
consumables.notes: Roll and Tip technique per FFD SS15.6. Mini roller applies material evenly to door/drawer slab faces, then tipped with angled sash brush. Foam rollers for ultra-smooth finish, microfiber for slightly more texture. One per coat application.

consumables.name: Airless/HVLP spray tip 310-412 (fine finish)
consumables.specification: Airless spray tip, 310-412 range (6-8 inch fan, 0.010-0.012 orifice) for fine-finish cabinet/trim
consumables.notes: Fine-finish spray tips for cabinets. Tight fan pattern for frame width and door/drawer faces. Fine atomization for smooth finish on scrutinized surfaces. One tip per ~20 gallons. Replace when pattern degrades or exhibits tails.

consumables.name: Spray gun filter
consumables.specification: In-line filter for airless spray gun
consumables.notes: Replace when clogged or every ~50 gallons. One per spray setup.

consumables.name: Screw extractor set
consumables.specification: Screw extractor bit set for stripped/painted-over screws
consumables.notes: RP-conditional: for painted-over stripped screws on cabinet hardware. Previous painters commonly painted over hinge screws and pull screws — paint fills screw head slots causing stripping during removal. One set per project, reusable. Not used in NC (new hardware, clean screws).

consumables.name: Flexible putty knife
consumables.specification: Flexible putty knife, 1.5-inch or 2-inch
consumables.notes: For applying lightweight spackle and wood filler to defects, dings, and scrape edges. Flexible blade for flush fill on cabinet surfaces. One per crew, reusable.

consumables.name: Painting pyramids / painter points
consumables.specification: Plastic painter's pyramids for elevating doors/drawers during painting
consumables.notes: Elevate removed cabinet doors/drawers during spray painting for full-surface access. 4 per door (standard configuration). Reusable across all doors/drawers. Spray method removes doors from hinges for horizontal spray on sawhorses.

consumables.name: Zip-lock bags for hardware storage
consumables.specification: Gallon-size zip-lock bags for hardware storage and labeling
consumables.notes: For bagging and labeling removed cabinet hardware (hinges, pulls, knobs, strike plates). One bag per cabinet door/drawer. Label with cabinet location for accurate reinstall. Essential for occupied-home cabinet work — mismatched hardware causes homeowner complaints.

consumables.name: Blue painter's tape 1.5-inch
consumables.specification: Blue painter's tape, 1.5-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: Multi-purpose masking tape for countertop edge masking, backsplash edge masking, wall edge masking, floor protection edges, and attaching masking paper/plastic. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 180 LF (60 yards) per roll regardless of width. Usage is heavy in cabinet RP due to 9+ protection zones.

consumables.name: Safe-release masking tape (yellow)
consumables.specification: Safe-release masking tape, yellow, for delicate surfaces
consumables.notes: For masking on delicate finished surfaces — countertop edges (especially natural stone), finished wall paint. Lower adhesion than blue tape to prevent surface damage during removal. Critical for countertop protection on granite/marble/quartz.

consumables.name: Masking paper 12-inch
consumables.specification: Masking paper, 12-inch width, 180 LF per roll (60 yards)
consumables.notes: For wall masking adjacent to cabinet work area during spray application. 12-inch width covers wall surface adjacent to upper and lower cabinets. Attached with blue tape. Per Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine: 180 LF (60 yards) per roll. Spray method only — brush method uses tape line only.

consumables.name: Plastic masking film/sheeting (1-2 mil)
consumables.specification: Plastic masking film/sheeting, 1-2 mil, for wall/ceiling/appliance spray protection
consumables.notes: Wall, ceiling, and appliance overspray protection for spray application. Drape over appliances (refrigerator, range, dishwasher, microwave), cover wall surfaces beyond masking paper range, ceiling masking. Spray method generates significant overspray in enclosed kitchen space.

consumables.name: Rosin paper (36-inch roll)
consumables.specification: Rosin paper roll, 36-inch width, for countertop and floor protection
consumables.notes: Primary countertop protection layer. Kraft/rosin paper covers countertop surface area. Also used for floor protection in cabinet work zone. Tear-resistant when wet (paint drips). For countertops: paper + plastic sheeting for spray, paper + tape for brush.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloth
consumables.specification: Canvas drop cloth, 4x12 ft runner or 4x5 ft compact
consumables.notes: Floor protection at cabinet base for brush method drip containment and sawhorse/door staging area. Runner-style for along cabinet base, compact for door staging. RP always has finished floors — floor protection is mandatory. 2-3 per kitchen.

consumables.name: Kraft paper for countertop protection
consumables.specification: Heavy-weight kraft paper, 36-inch width roll, for countertop surface protection
consumables.notes: CRITICAL: countertop protection is high-value (granite, quartz, marble). Kraft paper provides cushioned protection layer under plastic sheeting. Tape edges with safe-release tape (CON_MASKING_TAPE_SAFE_RELEASE) to prevent adhesive damage to stone surfaces. RP always has countertops installed.

consumables.name: Denatured alcohol
consumables.specification: Denatured alcohol for shellac cleanup
consumables.notes: Required for cleaning brushes and tools used with shellac stain-blocking primer (BIN). Standard water cleanup does NOT work for shellac. One quart per project. Conditional on smoke damage substrate state.

consumables.name: Pin-Type Moisture Meter
consumables.specification: Pin-type moisture meter for wood moisture content assessment
consumables.notes: For moisture assessment on base cabinet floors, back walls, and bath vanity surrounds during assessment phase. Reusable tool — shared across cabinet RP projects. Essential for identifying hidden moisture damage in base cabinets. Also used for moisture gate verification (confirm moisture source resolved before mildew primer).

floor_full_kitchen.description: Full kitchen floor coverage for cabinet spray work. Canvas drop cloths + rosin paper + tape edges

floor_perimeter.description: Drop cloth runners at cabinet base for brush method drip containment

countertop_covers.description: CRITICAL: high-value countertop surface protection (granite, quartz, marble). Always installed in RP
countertop_covers.notes: Kraft paper base + plastic sheeting for spray. Paper + safe-release tape for brush. Always present in RP — countertops are always installed in occupied kitchens.

backsplash_mask.description: Tile backsplash masking between counter and upper cabinets
backsplash_mask.notes: Always present in RP kitchen. Tape backsplash top edge and paper/tape bottom edge at countertop junction.

wall_adjacent_cabinet.description: Wall masking adjacent to cabinet work area for spray overspray protection
wall_adjacent_cabinet.notes: In RP, walls are ALWAYS finished — masking is mandatory for spray. Paper at edges, plastic for broader coverage.

ceiling_spray.description: Ceiling masking for spray overspray protection in kitchen work area

appliance_covers.description: Full appliance protection — ALWAYS required in RP (appliances always present in occupied homes)
appliance_covers.notes: RP MODIFICATION: always present in RP (was conditional/atypical in NC). Cover refrigerator, range, dishwasher, microwave. 4-mil plastic for tear resistance during work.

cabinet_hardware.description: Hardware removed, bagged, and labeled. RP adds scoring/extraction complexity for painted-over hardware
cabinet_hardware.notes: All hardware removed for RP cabinet painting. Score paint film around hinge barrels and screw heads before removal. Painted-over hardware adds ~30-50% to removal time vs NC.

plumbing_electrical.description: Plumbing fixtures in sink base cabinet, electrical outlets/switches near cabinets
plumbing_electrical.notes: Plumbing pipes/valves in sink base masked. Electrical outlet/switch plates removed and bagged. Under-cabinet lighting masked or removed.

contents_staging.description: RP-NEW: Cabinet contents must be emptied before painting. Staging area protection for contents
contents_staging.notes: Homeowner typically handles emptying cabinets. Painter verifies all cabinets are empty before starting. Contents staged in adjacent room on protected surface. Does not exist in NC.

compatibility_rules.description: Adhesion primer (SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT) under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Water-based adhesion primer is compatible with all fine-finish topcoat chemistries. Scuff sand primer before finish coats.

compatibility_rules.description: Bonding primer (SYS_PRIMER_BONDING_FACTORY) under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Bonding primer (Stix, XIM UMA) is compatible with all topcoat chemistries. Post-primer adhesion test recommended before proceeding.

compatibility_rules.description: Shellac stain blocker (SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT) under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Shellac seals stains and is compatible with all topcoat chemistries. Universal undercoat.

compatibility_rules.description: Mildew primer (SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT) under any fine-finish system
compatibility_rules.notes: Latex-based mildew primer is compatible with all fine-finish topcoat chemistries.

compatibility_rules.description: Double-dimension primer routing: condition state drives primer for painted surfaces
compatibility_rules.notes: When factory_finish_type is painted_latex or painted_oil, primer routing is condition-driven: SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT + painted_latex may skip primer. SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT + painted_oil requires adhesion primer MANDATORY. SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT and SS_INT_PEELING always require adhesion primer regardless of paint type.

compatibility_rules.description: Double-dimension primer routing: factory finish type drives primer for factory surfaces
compatibility_rules.notes: When factory_finish_type is lacquer, catalyzed_varnish, thermofoil, or unknown, bonding primer is MANDATORY regardless of condition state. Standard adhesion primer will NOT adhere to these surfaces.

compatibility_rules.description: Smoke damage overrides factory finish type routing — shellac BIN mandatory
compatibility_rules.notes: SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE always routes to shellac stain blocker regardless of factory finish type. Smoke encapsulation requirement supersedes all other primer routing. May need bonding primer UNDER shellac if factory lacquer + smoke damage (rare scenario).

compatibility_rules.description: Moisture damage routes to mildew primer — gate condition on moisture source
compatibility_rules.notes: SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE routes to mildew-resistant primer. Active moisture source must be resolved by other trades and biocide treatment must be completed before priming. Primarily under-sink base cabinets and bath vanity.

compatibility_rules.description: No primer skip for sound painted latex — only valid primer bypass scenario
compatibility_rules.notes: Primer may be skipped ONLY when ALL conditions are met: sound paint + painted latex + adhesion test passes + existing sheen is satin or lower. Any semi-gloss+ existing sheen, oil-based coating, factory finish, or marginal adhesion test REQUIRES primer. This is the ONLY scenario where primer can be skipped in cabinet RP.

compatibility_rules.description: Thermofoil bonding primer requires adhesion test gate — go/no-go before priming
compatibility_rules.gate_description: Inspect all edges, corners, and heat-exposed areas for lifting/bubbling. If delamination found: STOP — cabinet replacement required, not paintable. If intact: 120-grit mechanical scuff + bonding primer + ASTM D3359 adhesion test on primer.
compatibility_rules.notes: Thermofoil assessment gate is unique to cabinet RP. No other RP spec has a paintability gate assessment. Chemical degloss PROHIBITED on thermofoil — solvents damage vinyl wrap.

compatibility_rules.description: Cabinet interiors always QT3 — AWI semi-exposed standard
compatibility_rules.notes: Cabinet interiors always use SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3) regardless of exterior tier selection. Per AWI semi-exposed standard. Carries over from NC unchanged.

compatibility_rules.description: Sheen/QT gate — gloss requires QT5, semi-gloss requires QT4+
compatibility_rules.notes: Gloss available only at QT5. Semi-gloss available at QT4 and QT5. Satin available at all tiers (QT3+). Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine sheen/QT gate.

compatibility_rules.description: Spray is primary method for cabinet finish — brush is Roll and Tip alternative
compatibility_rules.notes: Spray strongly preferred per Fine Finish Doctrine SS10.3 and SS15.1.2. Spray ~1.4-2.0x faster than brush. Cabinet interiors are spray-only in practice (access constraints). 'brush' method means Roll and Tip technique per SS15.6 — NOT pure brush on flat surfaces.

compatibility_rules.description: QT5 brush requires 3 finish coats per FFD 15.10.3
compatibility_rules.notes: QT5 + brush triggers third finish coat per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 + spray remains at 2 finish coats. QT3 and QT4 always 2 finish coats regardless of method.

risk_notes.topic: Adhesion failure on factory lacquer cabinets
risk_notes.risk: Applying latex paint or standard primer directly over factory lacquer/catalyzed varnish without bonding primer. Factory lacquer is extremely hard and non-porous — standard primers have zero adhesion.
risk_notes.mitigation: Coating identification in assessment phase (xylene softens lacquer). Bonding primer (Stix, XIM UMA) mandatory for lacquer/catalyzed varnish. ASTM D3359 adhesion test on bonding primer before finish coats.

risk_notes.topic: Thermofoil painting failure — delamination within 6 months
risk_notes.risk: Painting over thermofoil without proper adhesion test gate or using chemical degloss (solvents damage vinyl).
risk_notes.mitigation: Thermofoil assessment gate: inspect edges/corners/heat areas. If delaminating: STOP, replacement required. If intact: 120-grit mechanical scuff only + bonding primer + adhesion test.

risk_notes.risk: Inadequate grease removal before priming. Grease film prevents adhesion and bleeds through waterborne paint.
risk_notes.mitigation: TSP/degreaser wash mandatory for ALL kitchen cabinet RP. Verify clean by wiping with white cloth. Multiple wash passes for heavy accumulation above range.

risk_notes.risk: Applying latex topcoat directly over oil/alkyd existing finish without adhesion primer. Oil-based paint was common on kitchen cabinets through the 1990s.
risk_notes.mitigation: Coating ID test (mineral spirits dissolves alkyd) during assessment. Adhesion primer mandatory when oil-based identified.

risk_notes.risk: Using latex primer instead of shellac stain blocker on smoke-damaged cabinets. PVA/acrylic primers have zero stain blocking capability (RC-002).
risk_notes.mitigation: Smoke assessment during condition inspect. Shellac BIN for smoke damage — full surface encapsulation. Two coats BIN for heavy nicotine.

risk_notes.topic: Finish blocking on reinstalled cabinet doors
risk_notes.risk: Insufficient cure time before door reinstallation. Doors closing against frame causes finish to bond and peel (blocking).
risk_notes.mitigation: MANDATORY 5-7 day minimum cure (7-14 days for waterborne alkyd at QT4). Verify cure by thumbnail test before reinstall. Do NOT shortcut cure period.

risk_notes.topic: Moisture damage recurrence under sink base cabinet
risk_notes.risk: Painting over moisture-damaged cabinet without resolving moisture source.
risk_notes.mitigation: Moisture source resolution is a gate — do NOT proceed until plumbing leak/condensation is fixed. Moisture meter check on base cabinet. Biocide treatment + mildew primer.

risk_notes.risk: Paint, solvent, or abrasive damage to high-value countertop surfaces (granite, quartz, marble).
risk_notes.mitigation: CRITICAL protection zone: kraft paper + plastic + safe-release tape. Verify protection integrity after each coat. Remove protection carefully to avoid pulling paint from freshly coated surfaces.

risk_notes.risk: Stripping screw heads or damaging hinge mortises during hardware removal from painted-over cabinets.
risk_notes.mitigation: Score paint film around hinge barrels and screw heads before removal. Use screw extractor for stripped screws. Account for paint build-up thickness in mortise depth.

risk_notes.topic: Brush marks on cabinet doors at brush method
risk_notes.risk: Overworking finish material on cabinet door faces — highly visible defect on scrutinized surface.
risk_notes.mitigation: Roll and Tip technique per FFD SS15.6. Apply, tip once, walk away per FFD 15.3.1. Modified urethane (BM Advance) STRONGLY recommended for open time.

material_notes.selection_guidance: Material system selection follows a TWO-DIMENSION routing model unique to cabinet RP: (1) CONDITION STATE drives primer for previously painted surfaces (adhesion, stain-block, mildew), (2) FACTORY FINISH TYPE drives primer for factory-finished surfaces (bonding for lacquer/thermofoil/catalyzed varnish). Finish system selection is QT-driven: QT3 = SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC, QT4 = SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE, QT5 = SYS_FF_PREMIUM. All items use the same finish system. Cabinet interiors always QT3 (AWI semi-exposed standard).

primer_routing_summary.painted_latex_sound: Skip primer OR SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT (conditional on adhesion test + existing sheen)
primer_routing_summary.factory_lacquer: SYS_PRIMER_BONDING_FACTORY (MANDATORY — standard primer will not adhere)

material_notes.coverage_variability: Cabinet coverage is mixed UOM (doors EA ~6 SF, drawers EA ~3 SF, frames SF direct, interiors SF direct). Primer coverage varies by system: adhesion 425 SF/gal, bonding 475 SF/gal, stain-block 325 SF/gal, mildew 400 SF/gal. Finish coverage is 400 SF/gal for all systems (post-prime substrate is equivalent). Interior coverage is 5-10% lower due to enclosed box spray waste.
material_notes.rp_vs_nc_differences: RP uses 4 state/factory-finish-driven primers (SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT, SYS_PRIMER_BONDING_FACTORY, SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT, SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT) instead of NC's 7 substrate-driven primers for bare wood/MDF. RP primer coverage is higher than NC because previously painted/factory surfaces absorb less than bare wood. RP adds TSP degreaser, heavy-duty kitchen degreaser, chemical deglosser, biocide spray, screw extractor, contour sanding sponge, assessment kit, and moisture meter not needed in NC.
material_notes.open_time_by_chemistry: Standard acrylic enamel has moderate open time. Modified urethane/waterborne alkyd (Advance, Emerald Urethane) has SHORT open time (5-10 min) — do not overwork per FFD 15.3.1.
material_notes.coat_count_summary: QT3-QT4: 2 finish coats standard. QT5 brush: 3 finish coats per FFD 15.10.3. QT5 spray: 2 finish coats. Prime coat (when applicable) is always 1 coat. Total coats: 2-4 depending on condition/QT/method.

assumptions.value: Door = 6 SF equivalent, drawer = 3 SF equivalent
assumptions.source: Standard residential cabinet dimensions — same as NC cabinet spec
assumptions.note: Industry standard EA-to-SF equivalents for cabinet components.

assumptions.value: RP adhesion primer at 425 SF/gal vs NC bare-wood primer at 350-400 SF/gal
assumptions.source: Previously painted surfaces absorb less primer than bare wood
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines RP vs NC primer coverage differential. Derived from product PDS and door RP precedent (COV_DIRP_PRIMER_ADHESION at 425 SF/gal).

assumptions.source: Factory finish surfaces are non-porous — minimal absorption
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines bonding primer coverage on factory finishes. Estimated 10-15% higher than adhesion primer based on near-zero substrate absorption.

assumptions.source: Shellac products have higher solids content
assumptions.note: Consistent with door RP stainblock profile (COV_DIRP_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK at 325 SF/gal).

assumptions.source: Field practice estimate for kitchen grease cleaning
assumptions.note: TSP yield for cabinet RP is different from door RP (30 doors/qt) because kitchen cabinets require more extensive grease wash with heavier concentration.

assumptions.value: 72 LF per tube (same tube yield) with 15-30% of joints needing replacement
assumptions.source: Materials_and_Consumables_Doctrine caulk section + RP selective replacement logic
assumptions.note: RP assesses and replaces only deteriorated caulk joints. Tube yield is same as NC but fewer tubes needed per project.

assumptions.value: 20-30% additional material consumption for enclosed cabinet box geometry
assumptions.source: Spray waste in enclosed spaces — same as NC assumption
assumptions.note: Enclosed box geometry causes spray bounce-back and overshoot waste. Consistent with NC coverage profile notes.
